title: Admin Role - Secondary School Based
description:
Location: Tonypandy, RCT
Start Date: ASAP
Contract Type: Part-Time 2 Days Per Week
Salary: £86 £90 per day

Are you an organised and efficient Administrator looking for a rewarding part-time role?

Do you have excellent communication skills and the ability to manage multiple administrative tasks in a busy office environment?

Are you a friendly, approachable individual who enjoys working as part of a supportive team?

TeacherActive is proud to be working with a welcoming Secondary School in Tonypandy, who are looking for a reliable and organised School Administrator to join their office team on a part-time basis.

The successful candidate will work 2 days per week, providing essential administrative support to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the school office. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with strong organisational skills who enjoys working in a busy and varied environment.

Key Responsibilities:
- Providing general administrative support to the school office team
- Answering telephone calls, responding to emails and handling enquiries professionally
- Maintaining accurate pupil records and updating school databases
- Supporting with attendance monitoring and general school administration
- Welcoming visitors and assisting pupils, parents and staff with enquiries
- Filing, scanning, photocopying and managing confidential documentation
- Supporting the wider administrative team with daily office duties

We are looking for an Administrator with the following:
- Previous experience in an administrative or office-based role
- Experience working within a school environment is desirable but not essential
- Excellent organisational and time management skills
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications
- A professional and friendly telephone manner
- The ability to manage confidential information appropriately
- A proactive attitude and willingness to support colleagues
- Availability to work 2 days per week

In return, you can expect:
- A dedicated team of consultants available 24/7 to support you
- A straightforward and easy onboarding process
- Competitive rates of pay between £86 and £90 per day
- Access to CPD and career development opportunities
- Opportunities for further work within local schools

If you are an enthusiastic and organised Administrator looking for a part-time opportunity in Tonypandy, we would love to hear from you!

Apply today to find out more about this exciting opportunity with TeacherActive.

All applicants will be contacted to discuss suitability and then invited to register with TeacherActive.

Registration involves an enhanced DBS check, ID checks and professional references. We pride ourselves on excellent service. We can provide a wide range of opportunities in schools and other educational institutions, with good rates of pay, at times to suit your needs.

About TeacherActive

TeacherActive is one of the UK s leading education recruitment agencies, with over 20 years of experience supporting schools and education professionals. We place teachers and support staff into a wide range of temporary, contract and permanent roles, helping candidates find rewarding opportunities that suit their experience, availability and career goals. We pride ourselves on providing an excellent service to both our schools and candidates.

Regular external audits have shown repeatedly that our standards are exceptional. We are passionate about finding the right staff for each education environment.

title: Client Support Executive
description:
Client Support Executive

Pontypridd - Office-based
Up to 30,000
Full-time, Permanent

About the Role

Yolk Recruitment is supporting a growing financial services business in Pontypridd with the recruitment of a Client Support Executive.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop their career within property finance and financial services. You will join a busy, customer-focused team, initially working closely with Relationship Managers to support clients throughout the lending process.

You'll play an important role in ensuring cases progress smoothly, providing excellent customer service and maintaining strong relationships with clients, brokers and other professional contacts.

Key Responsibilities
- Support Relationship Managers with the management of client cases from initial enquiry through to completion.
- Review and interpret key financial information, including credit searches, bank statements, financial accounts, property valuations and business appraisals.
- Manage a high-volume pipeline of cases while ensuring service standards and lending policies are followed.
- Build strong working relationships with brokers, customers, surveyors, solicitors and internal teams.
- Liaise with credit risk, finance, administration and other teams to ensure all lending requirements are satisfied.
- Handle telephone and email enquiries professionally and efficiently.
- Ensure all regulatory, compliance and internal policy requirements are followed.
- Check the accuracy and authenticity of client information and maintain detailed case records.
- Update and maintain accurate information on the company's case management system.
- Communicate information clearly and effectively to relevant internal and external stakeholders.
- Maintain an awareness of fraud prevention and associated risks.
- Provide consistently high levels of customer service throughout the lending process.

Experience
- Previous admin experience within finance or a legal setting would be ideal.
- Strong numerical and analytical skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to manage a busy workload and multiple cases simultaneously.
- Good time management and organisational skills.
- A self-motivated approach with the ability to work independently.
- The confidence to build positive relationships with customers and external stakeholders.
- A collaborative approach to working with colleagues across different teams.
- An interest in developing a career within financial services and property finance.

Benefits
- Basic Salary up to 30k
- Company bonus scheme
- Company pension
- 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, increasing with length of service
- Death in service benefit
- Multiple progression routes within the business

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:

Why not use your skills to make a difference and join our Home Tech Team in Cardiff. You'll be talking over the phone to customers with all sorts of home tech-related queries.

You don't need specific experience to join us. Provided you're naturally helpful, calm and can build relationships - we can train you on the rest.

We understand that life never stands still, and like most roles within EE, this opportunity is designed with flexibility in mind. What's in it for you?
- A great starting salary of £26,116 pro-rata rising to £26,738 pro-rata after 8 months of being here
- Online GP - Giving you access to a GP via telephone or video 24/7 for both you and your immediate family, fully funded by us
- Market leading paid carer's leave, up to 2 weeks off for carers to give that bit of extra support to our colleagues who are caring for family or friends who are disabled, ill or elderly
- Family Leave - Equalised maternity, paternity, and adoption leave and it gives all parents 18 weeks full pay and 8 weeks half pay in the first year however they choose to grow their family
- Huge discounts of EE & BT products including your Mobile and Broadband - saving you hundreds of pounds every year
- Support in carving your own career path. We are passionate about developing our people and we'll support you in achieving the career you want
- Season Ticket Travel Loan - Giving you the funds to pay for your travel to and from work up front, making a difference where it counts
- Volunteering days, so you can give back to your local community
- Optional Private Healthcare and Dental, to protect you and your family

On top of all that, we've got a great team culture, meaningful support and tailored training to help you build a lasting career. What are you waiting for?

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant - 9 - 12 Month Fixed-Term Contract

Pontypridd

Salary: £27,000 - £29,000 per annum, depending on experience

Môrwell Talent Solutions is working with a new client to recruit an experienced Accounts Assistant to join their finance team on an initial 9-12 month fixed-term contract. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a good understanding of transactional finance who enjoys being hands-on, getting involved in a variety of accounting duties and supporting a busy finance function.

Working closely with the Accounts Manager and Financial Controller, you will become an integral part of a small, close-knit team of four, providing day-to-day support across the accounts function and helping to ensure that financial processes run smoothly and efficiently. The successful candidate will ideally be available to start as soon as possible, although candidates with a shorter notice period will also be considered.

The Role

Reporting into the Accounts Manager and Financial Controller, your responsibilities will include:
- Processing high volumes of purchase ledger invoices using NetSuite.
- Matching, checking and accurately entering supplier invoices onto the system.
- Reconciling supplier statements and investigating any discrepancies.
- Dealing with supplier queries and resolving invoice-related issues.
- Preparing invoices for payment and supporting the payment run process.
- Undertaking general data entry and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Chasing outstanding payments and providing copy invoices and statements when requested.
- Providing some basic credit control support, including responding to customer and company queries.
- Liaising with companies, predominantly dealing with requests for copy invoices and account information.
- Providing general accounts administration and supporting the wider finance team with ad hoc duties as required.

About You

We are looking for someone who has previous experience in an Accounts Assistant or similar transactional finance role and is comfortable working in a busy environment where accuracy and attention to detail are important.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience working within an accounts or finance team.
- A good understanding of purchase ledger processes and transactional accounting.
- Experience processing invoices, reconciling supplier statements and dealing with supplier queries.
- Good data entry skills and the ability to manage a high volume of transactions accurately.
- Confidence using accounting systems. Experience with NetSuite would be advantageous, although training will be provided.
- Good working knowledge of Excel.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise your workload.
- A positive, flexible and hands-on approach to your work.

Just as importantly, you will be down to earth, reliable and hardworking, with a willingness to muck in and support your colleagues. This is a small team where everyone plays their part, so a helpful attitude and a genuine team-player mentality are essential.

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £27,000 - £29,000, depending on experience.
- An initial 9-12 month fixed-term contract.
- 20 days annual leave plus bank holidays.
- The opportunity to join a friendly, close-knit finance team.
- On-the-job training and support, including training on NetSuite.
- A Monday to Friday working week, 9.00am - 5.00pm.
- Four days office-based and one day working from home once fully trained and confident in the role.
- On-site parking and kitchen facilities.
- Access to a range of employee discounts, including offers on electrical goods, dining and shopping.
- Access to a flexible benefits programme, allowing employees to purchase items such as electrical goods and bikes, with payments deducted directly from their monthly salary.
- There may be the opportunity for the position to become permanent in the future; however, this cannot be guaranteed as the business is currently going through a period of restructuring.

Interested?

If you are an experienced Accounts Assistant looking for your next opportunity and are available at short notice, we would love to hear from you. Interviews will be taking place face to face as soon as possible, with a view to the successful candidate joining the business at the earliest opportunity. For further information or a confidential discussion, please contact Ceri or Sarah at Môrwell Talent Solutions.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
A well-established and growing manufacturing business in South Wales is seeking an experienced Accounts Assistant to join its finance team. Reporting directly to the Finance Director, this role offers an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership of the purchase ledger function whilst supporting wider finance operations within a fast-paced environment.

This position would suit a detail-oriented finance professional with strong organisational skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.

Key Responsibilities
- Processing high volumes of purchase invoices across raw materials, packaging and overhead expenditure.
- Preparing weekly and monthly supplier payment runs.
- Monitoring and reconciling Goods Received Not Invoiced (GRNI) balances.
- Performing regular supplier statement reconciliations.
- Monitoring and managing aged creditors.
- Managing and reconciling petty cash transactions.
- Raising purchase orders for indirect and overhead-related spend.
- Processing employee expense claims.
- Analysing expenditure across key cost areas, including utilities and distribution.
- Completing regular bank reconciliations.
- Supporting the wider finance function with additional duties as required.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
- Previous experience within an Accounts Assistant, Purchase Ledger or Accounts Payable position.
- Strong IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel.
- Experience working with integrated finance or ERP systems.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong organisational and analytical skills.
- The ability to work effectively within a busy finance environment.
- A proactive approach with a strong desire to deliver results and solve problems.
- Excellent communication skills and a collaborative, team-focused attitude.

What's on Offer
- The opportunity to join a stable and successful business with a strong market presence.
- A varied role with genuine responsibility and autonomy.
- Exposure to a broad range of finance activities.
- A supportive team environment with opportunities for ongoing development and progression.
- Competitive salary and benefits package.

title: HR Assistant
description:
HR Assistant / Administrator (Fixed-Term Contract)

Location: Aberdare
Contract: 6-Month Fixed-Term Contract
Hours: 16 hours per week, either:
- 2 full days per week, or
- 4 shorter days across the week

Salary: 28,000 - 35,000 pro rata, depending on experience

About the Role

We are seeking a proactive and organised HR Assistant / Administrator to join our client's team on a 6-month fixed-term contract. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous HR administration experience who enjoys providing day-to-day support within a busy HR function.

Working closely with the HR Manager, you will provide administrative and operational support across a broad range of HR activities, acting as a first point of contact for general HR queries and helping to ensure the smooth running of HR processes across the business.

Key Responsibilities
- Act as a first point of contact for general HR queries from employees and managers.
- Support the HR Manager with day-to-day HR administration and workload management.
- Assist with employee lifecycle processes, including onboarding, probation reviews, contractual changes, and offboarding.
- Maintain accurate employee records and ensure HR systems are kept up to date.
- Prepare HR documentation, including contracts, letters, and employment-related correspondence.
- Provide support to hiring managers throughout the recruitment process.
- Coordinate interviews and assist with recruitment administration where required.
- Support employees and managers with HR policies, procedures, and general guidance.
- Assist with absence management, annual leave tracking, and other HR reporting requirements.
- Ensure all HR administration is completed accurately and in line with company policies and employment legislation.

Person Specification
Essential
- Previous experience in an HR Administration, HR Assistant, or similar support role.
- Strong administrative and organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Confident communicator with the ability to build effective working relationships at all levels.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Outlook, Word, and Excel.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently.
- Professional and discreet approach when handling confidential information.

Desirable
- CIPD qualification or working towards CIPD accreditation.
- Experience supporting recruitment and onboarding processes.
- Knowledge of UK employment legislation and HR best practices.

What's on Offer
- Flexible working pattern of either 2 full days or 4 shorter days per week.
- Opportunity to gain broad HR experience within a supportive team environment.
- Competitive salary of 28,000 - 35,000 pro rata, depending on experience.
- Immediate opportunity to contribute and add value within a busy HR function.

title: Administrator
description: We are looking to recruit a friendly, enthusiastic and motivated Care Navigator to join our busy GP Practice team. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys working with people and thrives in a fast-paced environment. The role combines both reception and administrative duties, offering variety and the opportunity to develop a broad range of skills within primary care. No two days are the same, and you will play a vital role in ensuring patients receive the right support and access to the most appropriate services. The successful candidate will be involved in a wide range of reception, administrative and clinical support duties, including the management of patient enquiries, clinical correspondence, digital requests and routine healthcare administration. The role requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail and the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. As one of the first points of contact for our patients, the successful candidate will be expected to provide a professional, courteous and efficient service whilst always maintaining confidentiality. This is a varied role and duties will include, but are not limited to: Reception & Patient Contact Answering incoming telephone calls and assisting patients with enquiries. Greeting patients and visitors in a professional and welcoming manner. Booking, cancelling and amending appointments. Signposting patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional or service. Managing patient requests and queries. Patient Administration Processing patient registrations and updating patient records. Managing incoming and outgoing correspondence, including emails. Scanning and work flowing clinical correspondence. Summarising and coding patient records in accordance with practice procedures. Assisting clinicians and the wider practice team with administrative tasks. Clinical Administration & Digital Services Managing the Clinical Enquiries Inbox and actioning requests in line with practice protocols. Processing and allocating blood test results and other clinical workflow tasks. Processing online Fit Note (Med3) requests. Managing Subject Access Requests. Processing online requests received through MGC's digital services. Assisting with diabetic recall and administrative processes associated with long-term condition management. Supporting the referral process and liaising with hospitals and other healthcare providers. Processing private work requests. This is a varied and rewarding role that combines reception, administrative and patient support responsibilities. As one of the first points of contact for patients, you will play a key role in helping people access the right care and support whilst contributing to the smooth day-to-day running of the Practice. Duties will include: Welcoming patients and dealing with enquiries in person and by telephone. Booking and managing appointments. Care navigation and signposting patients to the most appropriate service. Managing patient requests and correspondence. Processing online consultations and patient requests. Managing the Clinical Enquiries Inbox. Processing test results and allocating blood test workflows. Supporting diabetic recall and long-term condition administration. Scanning and work flow clinical correspondence. Summarising and coding patient records. Supporting referrals and liaison with external healthcare providers. Processing private work requests and associated administration. Maintaining accurate records and ensuring confidentiality at all times. We are seeking someone who: Has excellent communication and customer service skills. Is confident using IT systems and learning new software. Can work efficiently in a busy environment. Has strong organisational skills and attention to detail. Is able to work both independently and as part of a team. Demonstrates professionalism, compassion and discretion. Previous NHS, healthcare or GP Practice experience is desirable but not essential, as full training will be provided. Full training and ongoing support. Opportunities to develop skills within Primary Care. A friendly and supportive working environment. The opportunity to make a real difference to patients' experiences. Additional hours and overtime opportunities may be available to cover annual leave, sickness absence and periods of increased demand. There are currently no antisocial hours or weekend working requirements. Applications will remain open until a suitable candidate is appointed. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should sufficient applications be received or a suitable candidate be identified. Previous applicants need not apply. If you are approachable, organised and committed to delivering outstanding patient service, we would love to hear from you.

title: Medical Receptionist
location: Llanbradach, CF83 3LR, CAERPHILLY, CF83 8ND, CAERPHILLY, CF83 8GL
description: **PLEASE NOTE - THIS JOB IS FOR OUR VILLAGE SURGERY PRACTICE** The Village Surgery are looking for a friendly and organised individual to join our team as a Receptionist on a temporary part time basis. This role is key to providing a welcoming and professional first point of contact for patients, visitors, and staff. Responsibilities include managing the reception desk, handling telephone enquiries, supporting administrative tasks, general office management tasks and ensuring smooth day-to-day operations. The ideal candidate will have excellent communication skills, a positive attitude, and the ability to work effectively in a busy healthcare environment. This position is temporary for 20 hours, worked on Thursday & Friday 08:00am-06:30pm. The role involves providing a professional, friendly and efficient reception service, welcoming patients, managing telephone and face-to-face enquiries, booking appointments and consultations, directing callers to appropriate healthcare professionals, taking messages and maintaining confidentiality. Undertake general administrative duties including opening and securing premises, processing mail, filing, scanning, photocopying, data entry and maintaining accurate records. Keep reception areas, noticeboards and leaflets tidy and presentable. Support clinical staff by arranging clinics, providing chaperone assistance and supporting emergencies where required. Manage the appointment system, including booking, amending and cancelling appointments, processing recalls, and accurately recording home visit requests. Maintain medical records, ensuring they are accurate, organised and securely managed. Process repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice procedures, maintain controlled drug prescription records and report death notifications appropriately. Prepare and maintain consulting rooms, ensuring they are clean, tidy, fully prepared for clinical sessions and secure at the end of each session. Provide flexible support across the practice, including sickness and annual leave cover, reasonable overtime and occasional weekend working. Undertake all statutory and mandatory training and any other reasonable duties requested by the management team or partners. Medical Receptionist Job Description Job Title: Medical Receptionist Responsible to: Practice Manager, Assistant Manager, Admin Manager Purpose of Role: To provide a first point of contact for patients and visitors whilst also carrying out general office management tasks. Job Responsibilities RECEPTION Receiving patients, consulting with members of practice team Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments,telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Taking messages and passing on information Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Answer the phone promptly with a calm, friendly tone; clearly state the practice name, listen actively, maintain confidentiality and ensure each caller feels respected, understood, and assisted efficiently. GENERAL ADMINISTRATION Opening up/locking up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with practice protocols Processing and distributing incoming and outgoing mail Filing and retrieving paperwork Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying, and scanning Keeping the reception area, noticeboards, leaflet etc. tidy and presentable Add clinics for allied staff if required Checking fridge temperature and recording accurately in writing and on to computer systems as required Chaperoning for GPs and Medical staff as required Aiding medical staff as needed during any emergency situations Cover sickness/annual leave and work reasonable overtime when required, including some weekends. Perform any other relevant and reasonable duties that may be requested by the Receptionist/Admin Manger, Practice Manager/Assistant Manager or partners. Undertake statutory and mandatory training as required. APPOINTMENT SYSTEM MANAGEMENT Book/edit/cancel appointments and recalls ensuring sufficient information is recorded to retrieve medical record. Monitor effectiveness of the system and report any problems or variations required. Deal with home visit requests, carefully noting all details. MEDICAL RECORDS MANAGEMENT Retrieve and refile records as required, ensuring that strict alphabetical order is adhered to. Ensure records are kept neat and tidy and in good repair with all necessary information recorded correctly on the outer cover. Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Maintaining and updating CD prescription records when needed Handing completed repeat prescriptions to patient and checking names and address. Report any death notifications to relevant staff by following practice procedure CONSULTATION ROOM PREPARATIONS Clearing consulting rooms as required Consulting rooms prepared in readiness for each consulting session. Rooms are checked at the end of each consulting session and left tidy and secure. Confidentiality: All staff are required to uphold strict confidentiality in accordance with the practices policies and relevant legislation Health & Safety: The employee will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risk involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Equality and Diversity: The employee will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and polices, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgemental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The employee will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record or own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Quality: The employee will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The employee should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communication effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services : The employee will:- Apply practice polices, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the polices, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participation in audit where appropriate
